V2 canManage() grants manage on the VIEW scope

`canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so an admin who only holds the all-groups `view` permission passes `canManage()`. The only caller is `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`GroupsResource.java:181`, `auth.groups().requireManage()`). That endpoint creates top-level groups and moves existing groups to top level (`realm.moveGroup(child, null)`, line 198). A view-only admin can therefore write. The V1 equivalent is MANAGE_USERS only, and the sibling `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79 correctly checks only `MANAGE`. The fix is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The Javadoc of `canManage()` in `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:75-76` says 'VIEW or MANAGE groups' and needs the same correction. `testViewGroups` never tries a write with only view-all-groups, so the tests do not catch this.

V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() never returns real group IDs

The lookup does not match how V2 stores group resources. (1) V2 per-group resources are named by group id and are created without a type (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121-127`). Only the type resource named "Groups" has type "Groups" (line 274). So `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` yields only that type resource. (2) The callback passes `groupResource.getId()`, the resource UUID, to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`. That method does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (line 141), which never matches a UUID, so it falls through to the all-groups check. If an all-groups permission with view-members/manage-members exists, the UUID of the type resource is added to `granted`. Otherwise the set is empty. Either way no real group id is returned. Effects for an admin who has view-members/manage-members on specific groups: `UsersResource.getUsersCount` calls `getUsersCount(realm, emptySet)`, which returns 0 (`JpaUserProvider.java:599-602`). `searchForUser` does not set `UserModel.GROUPS`, so the DB query is unrestricted and paginated over all users before the per-user `canView` filter. Pages come back short or empty. `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` passes only because the page is not full and `canViewByGroup` post-filters. To fix it, use the group id (the resource name) for both the permission check and the collected set, and make sure the lookup covers resources that have no type.

Missing negative and count/paging coverage for V2 group permissions

The tests check only positive outcomes plus a few initial 'forbidden' states. Missing cases: (a) an admin with only view-all-groups attempting to create a group, which would have caught the `canManage()` bug; (b) `users().count()` for an admin with a group-scoped view-members permission, which would have caught the empty `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` result; (c) membership management denied on a group that has no `manage-membership` permission. `testManageGroupMembership` checks only the allowed path after the initial forbidden check on a nonexistent group.

Javadoc references the wrong method / wrong return type

`requireManageMembers` says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but `GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers` (line 376) checks `canManageMembers`. The Javadoc on `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` (line 145) says it returns a 'Stream' while the method returns `Set<String>`.

Ambiguous provider sets no longer fail; a tie is resolved silently

The old code threw `IllegalStateException` when more than one `CryptoProvider` was on the classpath. Now the list is sorted by `order()` and the first entry wins, and the ignored providers are only logged at DEBUG (lines 64-70). `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return 200. If a FIPS or Elytron deployment also has `crypto-default` on the classpath by mistake, two providers tie at 200. The `sorted` call is stable, so the winner is whichever `ServiceLoader` returns first, which depends on classpath order. The server then starts with a possibly non-FIPS provider and logs nothing above DEBUG. The new `order()` only needs to let the authz-client provider (100) lose to a real one. Keep the fail-fast when the top two providers share the same `order()`, and throw the existing 'Multiple crypto providers' error in that case.

debugf called with a pre-built string as the format

`logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes the concatenated class names as a format string. The message also ends with a trailing ", ". Use `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` with a joined list, for example `Collectors.joining(", ")`.

Dead code: two encodings are built and discarded

Lines 114-115 create `ASN1Encoder` instances and write r and s, then throw the results away. The same encodings are rebuilt in the `return` statement at lines 117-121. Delete the two lines.

getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore provider, which becomes BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER

`BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` is a static final set from `getBouncyCastleProvider().getName()` (`common/.../BouncyIntegration.java:31-39`). With this provider it becomes the name of whatever JDK provider backs the default keystore type, probably "SUN". Any shared code that calls `X.getInstance(alg, BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER)` on this path would ask that provider for an algorithm it may not have, for example RSA `KeyFactory` or `Signature`. The `getKeyFactory`, `getSignature` and similar methods here throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, so that is the only path that can reach it today. The method name and the `KeyStore` lookup are misleading. Either return `null`, which `BouncyIntegration` handles by using `Security.getProviders()[0]`, or add a comment saying why the keystore provider is used.

First-wins init can lock in the stripped-down provider when jars sit in different classloaders

`CryptoIntegration.init` only detects a provider while `cryptoProvider == null`. It searches with `AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()`. If the authz-client jar is in a parent or shared classloader and the application's real provider (BC or FIPS) is only visible to a child classloader, this call runs first. It finds only `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` and sets it. A later `CryptoIntegration.init(appLoader)` then does nothing. Every other operation (`getKeyFactory`, `getSignature`, `getCertificateUtils` and so on) throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Was this layout considered? If it matters, `init` could be skipped when a provider is already set, or the context classloader could be tried first.

Round-trip test is self-consistent only and uses a P-256 key for ES384/ES512

The test checks `der -> RS -> der -> RS` and compares the two RS arrays. A consistent bug in the encoder and decoder would still pass, and the DER is never checked against the JDK. Verify `asn1Des` with `Signature.initVerify(publicKey).verify(asn1Des)` (the DER re-encoding is what `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` feeds to the verifier), and compare it to the original `sign`. The key is a default `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` key (P-256, line 42) for all three algorithms. ES384 and ES512 therefore only exercise 32-byte r and s zero-padded to 48 or 66 bytes. They never use a full-width value with the high bit set, which is the case that needs the leading 0x00 byte. Generate the key with the matching curve (`secp384r1`, `secp521r1`) and loop several times so short-r and high-bit cases occur. The tests also do not cover `ServiceLoader` selection or `order()` (authz provider loses to a real one), which is the other behaviour this change adds.

Reader thread is never joined and is not stopped if a delete fails

The reader thread is started with no `join()`, and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 is not in a `finally`. Two problems follow.

1. If any `remove()` at line 153 throws, `deletedAll` is never set. The thread then loops forever against the server and outlives the test.
2. On the success path, `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())` at line 157 runs without waiting for the thread's last in-flight `groups(...)` call. An exception from that call is added after the assertion and is lost. This is the final read, which is the one most likely to see an already-deleted group.

Fix: wrap the deletes in `try/finally` that sets `deletedAll`, keep the `Thread` reference, `join()` it with a timeout, and only then assert.

Test does not assert that any read overlapped the deletes

The test passes if the reader thread never completes a call while groups are being deleted. A count of successful or attempted reads, asserted to be above 0 and ideally started before the first delete, would show that the race was exercised. `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` uses the default `subGroupsCount=true`, so the path `GroupsResource.getGroups` → `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` → `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` is hit. The test should say what it targets. It currently has no comment or assertion tying it to the NPE in `getSubGroupsCount`.

Only getSubGroupsCount is made null-safe; the sibling delegations still NPE on a deleted group

`getSubGroupsStream(search, ...)` (lines 256, 262, 268) calls `modelSupplier.get().…` directly. `modelSupplier` wraps `getGroupModel()`, which returns null once the group is deleted, so these calls throw the same NPE under the same race. `getSubGroupsCount` now returns `null` in that case, so the REST representation silently omits `subGroupCount` instead of failing. `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount` returns `Long`, but the JPA implementation (model/jpa/.../GroupAdapter.java:190) always returns a value. Decide whether a vanished group should be skipped by the caller, as `GroupUtils.populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups` could do, or handled consistently in the adapter. The PR body says it fixes concurrent group access to prevent an NPE, but only this one method is covered.

Stray whitespace-only line and misspelled variable name

Line 117 holds trailing spaces. `groupUuuids` has three u's. Line 145 is an empty line at the start of the catch block.

Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without its UserModel argument

`UsernamePasswordForm` only declares `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160). A repo-wide grep finds no no-arg overload. `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, so the `services` module does not compile. Either pass `context.getUser()` here, or (preferred, see the other finding) make the helper take no argument.

`user != null` in the helper disables passkeys on the initial login form

`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` returns false when `user == null`. The old code set up WebAuthn data exactly when the user was NOT yet selected (the removed `context.getUser() == null` check in `challenge(...)` and the `else` branch of `authenticate`). Both call sites now use this helper (lines 115 and 137), so on a normal first-time login (user null) `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm` is never called. The conditional-UI challenge, rpId and `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` are missing from the page. That breaks auto-login with discoverable keys, the 'username webauthn' autocomplete and the passkey link, which the tests in this PR (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey`) expect. The same applies to the error re-render in `challenge(context, error, field)` after an invalid username: the passkey form is dropped. The intent of the change is to also cover users already set (re-authentication), so the condition should not depend on the user at all. Drop the parameter: `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled();`, and update the three call sites (including UsernameForm.java:47).

Missing @Override on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators

This method overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:128) but has no `@Override`. If the superclass signature changes, this override would silently stop applying, and the conditional UI would then show the user's authenticators again.

Util class now depends on the browser authenticator package, and a protected constant had to be made public

`AuthenticatorUtils` statically imports from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, which itself imports `AuthenticatorUtils`. That creates a package cycle, and the constant had to be widened from protected to public API. The check duplicates `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257). Consider keeping the helper on `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` as a public static method taking the context, so the constant stays protected.

Absence check relies on catching a broad Exception around findElement

The block `assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...)` inside `catch (Exception)` passes on any exception, not only `NoSuchElementException`. The sibling test in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest uses `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`, which is stricter. The same pattern is repeated at line 312.

Hung flusher process is no longer killed: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for SpawnProcess

The old `_ensure_process_alive` called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching ValueError). The new code only kills when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes here come from `self.mp_context.Process` (line 105), where `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`. That class is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which subclasses `BaseProcess` directly, not the generic `multiprocessing.Process` class. So I expect the isinstance check to be False and `kill()` to never run. I could not read the stdlib source in this checkout, which is why confidence is medium. The attribute's own annotation at line 68 names `SpawnProcess`, not `Process`.

When the cause is `hang`, the old process is still alive. `_create_process_for_shards` (line 259) then starts a second flusher for the same shards, and both run against the same Redis queues and share the same `healthy_since` and `backpressure_since` values. The hung process stays alive and can resume later, so the same segments can be produced to Kafka twice or the process can leak. The same check in `join` (line 346) means `terminate()` never runs there either. That one was already in the old code, but it should be fixed together.

Fix: check `isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` and skip those, or check `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. Do the same in `join`.

get_memory_info is run once per flusher process, and every call queries the whole Redis cluster

`SpansBuffer.get_memory_info` returns `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` (buffer.py:375-376), which calls `INFO` on every master node of the cluster, not just the shard's node (memory.py:82-105). With N flusher processes, `submit()` now makes N identical cluster-wide INFO sweeps. `submit()` is hit on every batch, and only when `max-memory-percentage < 1.0`. `used` and `available` are both multiplied by N, so the ratio stays correct and nothing is wrong, but the extra work is pure waste. Query the cluster once, for example with one buffer or the consumer's own `buffer`.

Inconsistent metric tag name ('shards' vs 'shard'), and a comma-joined string used as the tag value

`spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards`. `flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes` and `flusher_unhealthy` use `shard`. The `shard` tag also holds a comma-joined list such as "0,1,2,3" (line 144) in the produce and segment_size metrics, but a single shard id in `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244). Dashboards cannot join these series on one tag. Pick one name and one value format, for example a process index tag.

Dead code: _create_process_for_shard is unused, and `if not process` can never be true

`_create_process_for_shard` (lines 127-132) has no caller anywhere in the repository. The `if not process: continue` check (lines 222-223) is always False, because a Process or Thread object is always truthy and `self.processes` is only ever filled with started processes. Remove both.

Docstring says one process per shard, but the number of processes is capped by max_processes

The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard". The code creates `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes and shares shards between them round-robin (lines 60-66). The CLI default is `--flusher-processes 1`, so by default there is one process for all shards. Reword it to match. The `:param` list is also missing `max_processes`.

Invalid or empty values for flusher_processes are not validated

`max_processes or len(...)` turns 0 into 'one process per shard'. A negative `--flusher-processes` makes `num_processes` negative. With any assigned shards, `i % self.num_processes` then yields a key that is not in `process_to_shards_map`, and construction fails with a KeyError. The click option is a plain `int` with no `IntRange(min=1)`. Use `type=click.IntRange(min=1)` in `consumers/__init__.py:432-437`. Separately, with no assigned shards, `num_processes` is 0 and no flusher process starts at all. Before this change one was always started. That case is harmless, since there is nothing to flush.

The added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test patches time.sleep

Line 15 does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`. That replaces the `sleep` attribute of the `time` module, so `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 also does nothing. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process' describes behaviour that never happens, and the race between setting drift=9000 and `step.join()` setting `stopped` is unchanged. A flusher thread that has not yet looped past the drift change when `stopped` is set exits without flushing, and `(msg,) = messages` then fails. Use a bounded poll loop on `messages` with the real sleep (saved before patching). The added `transaction=True` marker is not explained anywhere.

The new test checks only the process/shard bookkeeping, not that multi-shard flushing or restarts work

`test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts the process count and that the shard counts sum to 4. It never sends spans through a flusher that owns several shards. It does not check that the shards are partitioned without overlap, and it does not exercise `_ensure_processes_alive` (restart, or the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS error) for per-process state. That is where the bug on flusher.py:254 sits. `messages` and `commits` are unused. Add a test with a crashed or hung process and one with spans on multiple shards.

Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay event timestamps (likely milliseconds)

`gen_request_data` interleaves errors and replay events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Error timestamps come from the nodestore event payload (`data.get("timestamp")`, line 115), which is epoch seconds. Replay recording events are rrweb events, whose timestamps are epoch milliseconds; the parser casts `payload["timestamp"]` to int and the replay code elsewhere treats them as ms. If so, every error is `<` the first replay event, so all errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of in chronological order. Seer then gets a wrong timeline with no error. The tests use `now.timestamp()` for both the error and the recording event (test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py ~149-188), so they would not catch a unit mismatch. Normalize the units (e.g. error ts * 1000, or compare both in seconds) and add a test with realistic ms replay timestamps. I did not find a conversion in `as_log_message`/`event_parser.py`; please confirm the unit of the stored recording timestamps.

zip(error_ids, events.values()) can pair IDs with the wrong events

`nodestore.get_multi` returns a dict that is deduplicated, omits missing nodes, and puts uncached ids before cached ones (nodestore/base.py:184-205). Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` therefore misaligns whenever an id is duplicated, a node is missing, or the result mixes cached and uncached entries. The `id` field of `ErrorEvent` can then belong to a different event than its title/message/timestamp. The id is not used in the log message today, so the visible effect is nil, but it is a latent bug. Key the lookup by node id: `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`.

Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled

`query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` (lines 70-84) run before the `enable_error_context=false` check at 87-92. When the caller disables error context, the ClickHouse aggregation query is still executed and its result is unused. Move the flag check ahead of the query and only query for `error_ids` when error fetching is enabled.

age/timestamp exclusivity is not enforced when both are absent or when age is 0

Field-level `validate_age`/`validate_timestamp` only run when that field is present, and both fields are `required=False`. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` therefore validates, although the comments say one of the two specs must be followed. The checks also use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` (valid per the spec: report generated just now) together with `timestamp` passes the 'mutually exclusive' check. Use a `validate()` method that checks `"age" in data` / `"timestamp" in data` and requires exactly one. The docstrings ('Validate that age is absent...') also describe the opposite of what each check does.

get_environment_info issues a Snuba query plus a DB query for every issue in the PR comment

`issue.get_recommended_event()` runs a Snuba query (models/group.py:870-890) and `get_environment()` then does `Environment.objects.get` (eventstore/models.py:176-185), once per issue inside the list comprehension in both the GitHub and GitLab `get_comment_body`. This adds N sequential Snuba round trips to the PR comment task, with no timeout of its own beyond the broad `except Exception`. Consider batching, or reading the environment from the group's event tags already fetched. Also note failures are logged at `info`, so a persistent Snuba failure would be invisible.

Flagged branch renders an empty table and ignores the query results

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is on, `TableWidgetVisualization` receives `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`, so the widget shows no data and drops `tableResults`, loading state, and title. I found no registration of this flag under src/sentry, so organizations cannot have it today, but anyone enabling it would see all dashboard table widgets blank. Either wire in `result.data`/`result.meta` or leave this out of the PR until the flag is registered.

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only applies while a search query is typed

`sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` unchanged at lines 61-63 when `searchQuery` is empty. The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check at line 67 sits after that early return, so `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown by default and are only hidden once the user types something. `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` is the only list passed to `AttributesTree` (line 139), so nothing else hides them. Apply the hidden-attribute filter before the early return, for example `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name))`.

Flex migration drops align-items and gap that the old Container/FlexBox had

The removed `FlexBox` was `display:flex; align-items:center; gap: space(1)`, and `Container` extended it with `justify-content: space-between`. The loaded state at line 93 is now `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">`, which loses both `align="center"` and `gap={space(1)}`. The tabs and `TraceContextVitals` are no longer vertically centred and have no gap between them. In `Placeholder`, the second inner `<Flex>` (line 27) also lost `align="center"` and `gap={space(1)}`, so the three 100px placeholders now touch each other. Add `align="center" gap={space(1)}` to both.

Rewrite to raw useQuery drops retry:false and staleTime, so errors keep isLoading true for several seconds

The old `useApiQuery` call set `retry: false`. The new `useQuery` (lines 50-54) sets only `enabled`, `queryKey` and `queryFn`. `DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG` (static/app/utils/queryClient.tsx:19-26) does not override `retry`, so react-query's default of 3 retries with backoff applies. `isLoading` is now `isFetching`, so when `/trace-items/attributes/` fails, the search builder and column editors show a loading state for the whole retry window. Restore `retry: false`. Also decide on `staleTime` explicitly, since the old code set `staleTime: 0`. The queryKey also has no org slug, though `getTraceItemAttributeKeys` uses `organization.slug`; consider adding it.

New SummaryListContainer grid item has no overflow/min-height, so the list may stop scrolling inside its row

Previously the `list` grid item was the `FluidHeight` Container, which has `overflow: hidden` and `height: 100%`, so it was clamped to the `1fr` row. The grid item is now `SummaryListContainer` (lines 125-129), a plain flex column with neither `overflow: hidden` nor `min-height: 0`. A grid item with `overflow: visible` has an automatic minimum height, so a tall `FeedbackList` could stretch the row and be clipped by `LayoutGrid`'s `overflow: hidden` instead of scrolling inside its own container. I did not run it. Add `overflow: hidden; min-height: 0` to `SummaryListContainer` and check list scrolling with the summary shown.

Flex replacement of FlexBox drops height: 100%

The old `FlexBox` was `flex-grow:1; flex-direction:column; height:100%`. `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` renders `flex: 1` (basis 0%) and no height. If the parent does not give a definite flex height, the waterfall container may size differently. Confirm the parent's layout, or keep an explicit height.

Typo and missing space in story copy Line 27 says "the the most basic example". Line 28 puts `tableData` straight after "requires" with no space, and lines 57-58 have the same problem with "type" and `TabularData`. JSX collapses the newline, so the text renders as "requirestableData" and "typeTabularData". Add `{' '}` after those words.

Flex.Item grow={1} is not equivalent to the removed `flex: 1`

The removed `FlexContainer` used `flex: 1`, which is `1 1 0%`. `Flex.Item grow={1}` renders `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: auto` (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:35-46). With `auto` basis the description column starts from its max-content width. The sibling `Metadata` (line 265) has `margin-left: 4 / margin-right: 100px` and also an auto basis, so when the description text is long the shrink is shared proportionally and `Metadata` can be squeezed. With the old `0%` basis the description only took the leftover space. `Flex.Item` accepts `flex={1}`, which renders `flex: 1` and keeps the old layout exactly.

Tests no longer cover the request-body logging or the non-list payload branch

The `logger.info("browser_report_received", ...)` assertions were removed from `test_basic` and the multi-report test, but the endpoint still logs the raw body (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:93), so that behavior is now untested. The non-list branch (lines 99-104, a bare 422 with no body) also has no test. The new validation tests only cover the per-report serializer path. A test that posts a dict instead of a list and expects 422 would cover it.

No test for a PUT that omits `owner`

`BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update` only touches the owner when `"owner" in validated_data` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:67). The three new tests cover set-to-user, switch-to-team and clear (`None`). None covers an update that leaves `owner` out, which must keep the existing owner. A regression such as treating a missing key like `None` would clear owners on every unrelated edit, and no test would catch it. Consider adding a case: set an owner, PUT `self.valid_data` without `owner`, and assert the owner is unchanged.

Two new tests duplicate ~60 lines of setup

`test_get_with_error` and `test_get_with_error_context_disabled` repeat the same code: storing the event, `store_replays`, building the recording segment and the feature block. Only the query param and the final assertions differ. A helper such as `_setup_replay_with_error()` or a `parametrize` over `enable_error_context` would cut the repetition and make the intended difference clear.

OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate a DateTimeField; the audit-log endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime"

`get_item_key` (l.838-840) is copied from `Paginator`, which is for numeric keys. It runs `math.floor(getattr(item, "datetime"))`, and `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). This raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])` on a non-empty page. `value_from_cursor` (l.842-843) also returns the raw cursor value, where `DateTimePaginator` converts it back to a datetime. The `build_queryset` filter would therefore compare the datetime column with an integer. `GET .../audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true` by an eligible user returns a 500 whenever the org has audit log rows. It needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key handling, for example by subclassing it, if the paginator is kept at all.

Negative offsets are passed to Django slicing, which asserts; the comments say the opposite

The comments at l.874-880 say the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" and that this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing: `queryset[-5:96]` raises `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. `Cursor.from_string` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53-61) accepts any integer offset from the `cursor` query parameter, for example `cursor=0:-5:0`. With `optimized_pagination=true` and an eligible user, a negative offset reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (l.882) and returns a 500. Nothing is gained either. The branch has no valid behaviour to offer, and its comment about "permissions checked at the queryset level" justifies reading rows outside the page bounds. Remove the branch and clamp or reject negative offsets.

TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex writes it concurrently

Strategy close() kills the factory-shared queue pool, so every message after a rebalance is dropped and its offset committed

`ResultsStrategyFactory` builds one `FixedQueuePool` in `__init__` (result_consumer.py:133) and hands that same instance to every strategy created in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` (result_consumer.py:254-259). Arroyo calls `create_with_partitions` again after each rebalance, and it closes the previous strategy first. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (lines 338, 342). That sets `worker.shutdown = True`, shuts every queue and ends the worker threads, and nothing recreates them. The factory still holds the dead pool, because `queue_pool` is only cleared in `ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown`. The next strategy therefore runs on a dead pool. In `submit`, `work_queue.put()` raises `queue.ShutDown`. The broad `except Exception` at line 317 catches it, logs it, then calls `add_offset` and `complete_offset` for that offset (lines 320-325). The commit loop then treats the offset as done and commits it. From the first rebalance on, every message is silently dropped and its offset committed. The other modes do not have this problem: `create_thread_parallel_worker` also uses a factory-owned executor, but closing `BatchStep` or `RunTask` does not shut that executor down. The tests never create a second strategy after closing the first, so none of them catches this.

The shared `OffsetTracker` is also never cleared on rebalance. Offsets for revoked partitions stay in it, and the commit loop passes them to `commit` in the same dict as the partitions that are still assigned. If arroyo rejects offsets for unassigned partitions (I did not check its source), one stale partition would make the whole commit fail every second. Reset or prune the tracker per strategy.

Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite what the docstring says

The `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring (line 253) promises "Natural backpressure when queues fill up". But every queue is `queue.Queue()` with no `maxsize` (line 185). `submit` never blocks and never raises `MessageRejected`, and `poll` only emits a gauge. Arroyo therefore keeps polling Kafka at full speed even when the workers are slower, for example during a DB slowdown. Queued `WorkItem`s, each holding the decoded result and the original message, grow without limit, which risks OOM. Offsets are only committed after processing, so a crash would replay everything. Either bound the queues and raise `arroyo.processing.strategies.abstract.MessageRejected` when the target queue is full, or drop the claim from the docstring and add a depth limit.

Commit stalls permanently on any non-contiguous offset

`get_committable_offsets` only advances across consecutive integers. The loop at lines 89-93 breaks at the first offset that is not in `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not always dense: log compaction and transaction markers leave gaps, and the consumer never sees those offsets. If a gap occurs, the committed offset stops there for good and `all_offsets` grows without bound, so the consumer is stuck without errors. `test_offset_gaps_block_commits` asserts this as the intended behaviour. The usual approach is to track offsets by submit order, not by integer adjacency. Commit up to the highest offset such that every offset submitted before it has completed, using a sorted or ordered structure of what was actually submitted.

Shutdown can block for about 100 seconds, and `join` repeats it

`FixedQueuePool.shutdown` joins each worker one after another with `timeout=5.0` (lines 242-243). Nothing makes the waits overlap, so with the default 20 workers all busy on slow DB work, the worst case is 20 × 5s. `close()` adds a 5s join of the commit thread first (line 337), for about 105s in total. `join(timeout)` ignores its argument and calls `close()` again (line 345), which can add another 100s. During a rebalance this blocks the consumer's poll loop for far longer than the usual Kafka `max.poll.interval.ms`, so the consumer may be kicked out of the group. Use a single shared deadline, for example `deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout` with `join(max(0, deadline - now))`, and honour the `timeout` argument in `join`. Also commit once more with the completed offsets on a clean close.

Commit function is called from a background thread

`_commit_loop` calls `commit_function`, which calls arroyo's `commit` callback (result_consumer.py:249-252), from a separate daemon thread while the main thread keeps polling and handling rebalance callbacks. Arroyo's commit callback normally runs on the processor thread, and I did not confirm that the Kafka consumer's staged-offset state is safe to use from two threads. Is this safe? If not, collect the committable offsets on the thread that calls `poll()` and commit there. That also removes the need for the 1s wake-up thread.

The docstring says errors in processing "don't block offset commits for other messages", but the test asserts that no commit for `test_partition` happened. If failed messages are meant to be committed (current behaviour, and what the docstring says), wait for the commit and assert `committed_offsets[test_partition] == 102`. The five results go through the real `UptimeResultProcessor`, since the processor is not patched. `factory.shutdown()` calls `queue_pool.shutdown()`, which drains the queues and joins the workers for up to 5s each, so real `handle_result` calls run in non-test threads. Tests never close the strategy, so each leaks a commit thread

Every new test calls `factory.shutdown()` but never `consumer.close()`. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` starts a daemon commit thread in `__init__` that loops until `shutdown_event` is set (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:268-291). `ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown` stops only the queue pool. All five results use the same subscription, so they always hit one FIFO queue and ordering is trivially preserved. A regression in the group-to-queue mapping would not be caught. Interleave results from a second subscription and assert per-subscription order. Also note that `send_result` builds every message with the same `Partition(Topic("test"), 1)` and offset 1, so these tests do not exercise offset tracking.

Legacy write goroutines derive their context from the request context

Fallback locales are preloaded only in controller requests, not in jobs or with_locale blocks

The fallback chain is now [locale, site default, :en] for every I18n.t. - `app/jobs/base.rb:151` sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` in every job thread.
- `app/services/post_alerter.rb:138` uses `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`.

A job running with a non-English site locale is the likely case. The result is silent. The fix is to preload the fallback chain wherever the locale is set, for example by making `load_locale` or `translate` load the whole fallback chain. At minimum, call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` after the locale assignment in `app/jobs/base.rb` and inside the `with_locale` block in `post_alerter.rb`.

Fabricator contents are in each other's files

"is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that

website_name leaks the website host that is hidden for restricted users

`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. Add a spec for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous scope.

Displayed website name goes stale after the user edits their website

website_name logic is fragile and drops information

Several problems in `website_name`:
- `URI(...)` is called three times, and `rescue nil` is a statement modifier that hides every error.
- A website with no scheme, such as `example.com`, parses with a nil host. No name is shown, and the user's link is still set. The old client code behaved the same way here, but now there is no fallback.
- `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` compares label counts. It treats unrelated hosts such as `a.example.com` and `b.other.org` as non-siblings. Siblings with a longer public suffix, such as `x.example.co.uk` and `y.example.co.uk`, also compare equal, but the check only works for these sibling cases.
- `"." << website_host` mutates a literal string; use `".#{website_host}"`.
- A path of `/` produces a trailing-slash name such as `example.com/`.
Parse once into a local variable and extract the comparison into a small helper.

Missing coverage for sibling-subdomain branch, invalid or blank website, and restricted viewers

The three examples cover only the same-host branch, the parent-domain branch, and the unrelated-domain branch. They do not cover the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (line 146 of the serializer). They do not cover a blank or invalid website, where `website_name` should be omitted. Unescaped embed URL in raw-HTML post: stored XSS and unauthenticated topic creation via /embed/best `import` interpolates `url` straight into `#{url}` and the post is then stored with `cook_method: raw_html` (line 22), so `Post#cook` returns the markup unsanitized (app/models/post.rb:133). The URL reaches here from the public `embed_url` param: embed_controller.rb:15 enqueues `retrieve_topic`, then TopicRetriever#fetch_http (lib/topic_retriever.rb:52) calls `import_remote`. The only checks are that the host equals `embeddable_host` (topic_retriever.rb:15) and that the URL matches `/^https?:\/\//` (topic_embed.rb:11). A `'` is legal in a URI query, so a request like `embed_url=http:///real-article?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` passes both checks. Most sites return 200 for the real article and ignore the query string. The footer link then breaks out of the attribute, and the stored post is served raw on the forum's own origin. Separately, `^` matches at any line start, so a multi-line string passes the regex. The `Referer` check in `ensure_embeddable` is not authentication, because any non-browser client can send that header. The `embed_url` is also the unique key, so any distinct query string makes a new topic: anyone can create unlimited topics. The per-URL throttle in TopicRetriever does not limit this. Fix: HTML-escape the URL in the footer (`ERB::Util.h` / `CGI.escapeHTML`). Use `\A…\z` in the scheme check. Normalize the URL (drop the query and fragment, or require it to match an expected pattern) before using it as the key. Consider rate-limiting creation per IP.

raw_html cook method bypasses all sanitization for third-party content

`return raw if cook_method == raw_html` skips the PrettyText pipeline, which is what sanitizes normal posts. The content comes from external sources and is not sanitized on the way in. In poll_feed.rb:35, `CGI.unescapeHTML` turns entity-encoded feed content into live HTML, including `<script>` and `on*=` attributes. `String#scrub` only repairs invalid bytes. In `import_remote` (topic_embed.rb:48-50), ruby-readability whitelists tags and the `href`/`src` attributes but does not filter `javascript:` URLs. Every viewer of the topic page and the embed iframe gets this HTML as-is. Sanitize the raw HTML on import, or run the cooked output through the existing sanitizer (e.g. `PrettyText.sanitize`-style whitelist) instead of returning `raw` verbatim.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs and skips path-relative ones

For `href`/`src` starting with `/`, the code strips all leading slashes and prefixes the embed site's host. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png` becomes `http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which is a broken link or image. URLs without a leading slash (`images/a.png`, `../x`) are left untouched, although the comment says relative URLs are converted. Use `URI.join(url, href)` (or `URI(url).merge(href)`) and keep the original value if parsing raises. Add a test for `//host/x` and for a path-relative URL.

Anonymous page cache bypasses the referer check and caches a referer-specific page

`discourse_expires_in` makes AnonymousCache store the 200 response for 1 minute, along with its headers including `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. The cache key is only host plus REQUEST_URI (lib/middleware/anonymous_cache.rb:14), and the middleware answers before the controller runs. After one legitimate request, any anonymous request for the same `embed_url` gets the page with ALLOWALL regardless of its Referer, so `ensure_embeddable` is skipped. The cached layout also contains the first requester's `request.referer` as the postMessage targetOrigin (layouts/embed.html.erb:11). A request from a different scheme or port in the next minute gets a message that the browser silently drops, so the iframe height is never set. Either vary the cache key on the referer, or don't cache the embed, or make the check independent of the cached page.

One feed item without content aborts the whole poll

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content` (SimpleRSS returns nil for RSS items that only have `description`). The exception propagates out of `each` (the job has `retry: false`), so the remaining items are never imported on this run or later ones. The same happens if `TopicEmbed.import` raises for one item. Fall back to `i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item with a log line.

Unbounded network fetches with no overall timeout or size limit

`open(url).read` here, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in poll_feed.rb:29, and `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` called from TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41) all use open-uri. It has only Net::HTTP's per-read timeout, so a slow-drip server holds the worker indefinitely, and there is no response-size cap. The RetrieveTopic job also imports the whole feed synchronously. When `SiteSetting.queue_jobs?` is false, `Jobs.enqueue` runs the job inline (app/jobs/base.rb:168-172), so `/embed/best` blocks the web request for that whole time. Wrap the fetches in `Timeout.timeout` (or pass `read_timeout`/`open_timeout`) and cap the body size.

--category option removed, so imports can no longer target a category

The `-c/--category` option and its lookup were deleted, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (called at line 148) has no category parameter. Users who pass `-c` get a Thor error. Either keep the option and thread `category` through `import_remote`/`PostCreator`, or state in the PR that it is dropped on purpose.

create_table force: true drops any existing table

`force: true` runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first, so re-running the migration (`db:migrate:redo`, a rollback and re-apply, or a restored DB with a partial schema) silently deletes all `topic_embeds` rows. The same flag was added to the already-shipped `create_top_topics` migration (20131223171005 line 3). Drop `force: true` from both. Also, `topic_embeds` has no index on `topic_id` or `post_id`.

Whitespace-only edits to an old migration

The diff only strips trailing whitespace and removes the final newline of an already-shipped migration. It is unrelated noise. Revert it.

NOT NULL column with a default on posts rewrites and locks the table on older PostgreSQL

`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` rewrites the whole `posts` table under an exclusive lock on PostgreSQL before 11. On large forums that blocks reads and writes for the duration. Consider adding the column nullable, then setting the default and backfilling in batches.

`<%- end if %>` is a dangling modifier

`end if` with no condition is not valid on its own. It only parses because the condition continues onto the next line, which is whatever statement the ERB compiler emits next (an output-buffer append). It works by accident and depends on the template compiler's output. Use `<%- end %>`.

Origin check uses substring match; missing container is unhandled

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`, such as a prefix or an empty string. Compare `e.origin` exactly with the origin of `discourseUrl`. Separately, `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` can be null, and then `comments.appendChild` throws with no hint to the embedding site. Also check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

Throttle is not atomic

`setnx` followed by a separate `expire` leaves a key with no TTL if the process dies between the two calls. That URL is then never retrieved again. Use `$redis.set(key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)`, or call `expire` unconditionally.

Tests miss the risky paths

The update test only checks that the text matches. It does not check that `content_sha1` changed, that no second topic or embed was created, or that an unchanged re-import does nothing. There is no test for a URL containing quotes in the footer, for protocol-relative or path-relative links, or for HTML sanitization of raw_html posts. poll_feed_spec.rb never exercises `poll_feed` itself (parsing, `link`/`id` fallback, nil content). The `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` there is unused. The controller spec has no case for a referer on the wrong host.

Are the new gems in Gemfile.lock?

A search of Gemfile.lock at the head found no `simple-rss` or `ruby-readability` entries. If the lockfile is committed, it needs updating, or deployments with a frozen bundle will fail. Is it updated in this PR?

Second `self.downsize` replaces the first, so `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` now raises ArgumentError

Ruby has no overloading. The `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the 5-argument version at line 145, which is now dead code. Its signature takes 3 required arguments plus 1 optional hash, so at most 4 arguments.

The existing caller `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments. That raises `ArgumentError`, so the job fails and uploaded custom emoji are never downsized to 100x100. The other callers (`OptimizedImage.resize` in `lib/letter_avatar.rb:48` and `app/models/upload.rb:98`) are unaffected.

Hard-coded 10MB client limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and caps admin-raised image limits

Before this change, `validateUploadedFile` read `max_<type>_size_kb`, so it applied `max_attachment_size_kb` to attachments. Now every file gets 10MB.

- Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` but under 10MB pass the client check. They are uploaded and only rejected server-side. The server also downsizes only images, so attachments get no such leniency.
- Admins who raised `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB (for example `script/import_scripts/tnation.rb:115-116`) are now blocked client-side. The server would accept those files.
- Line 246 has the same problem for the 413 alert. It reports `10240` for any file type, even when the real limit is lower.

Fix: keep the setting for attachments, as in `type === 'image' ? 10 * 1024 : Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb`. Better, use `Math.max(10 * 1024, max_image_size_kb)` for images. In the 413 branch, use the matching setting, not a constant.

Downsize loop does not handle animated GIFs, SVGs or a failed conversion

The loop ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, which is `false` when the command fails (`optimized_image.rb:160-163`). It therefore always runs 5 times on a failing image.

For a `.gif` with `allow_animated_thumbnails` on, `optimize` switches to `downsize_instructions_animated` (`optimized_image.rb:137-138`, `155`). That emits `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, but gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects `WxH`, not a percentage. I'm relying on my knowledge of gifsicle here and did not run it. The conversion would fail on every attempt and the oversized GIF would fall through to the validator.

`FileHelper.is_image?` (`lib/file_helper.rb:5`) also matches `.svg`. Running ImageMagick `-resize 80%` on an SVG, in place, rasterizes it or corrupts it.

Fix:
- Exclude SVG from the loop.
- Break when `downsize` returns false.
- Use a percentage-safe path for animated GIFs, or skip them.

10MB cap is not enforced server-side for multipart uploads, and the loop runs ImageMagick on unbounded input

The 10MB limit is applied only to API URL downloads (line 55) and in the client JS (`utilities.js`). A multipart upload takes `file.tempfile` unchecked, so the only bound is the web server's `client_max_body_size`.

The new block then runs up to 5 in-place `convert` passes on whatever image was posted. Each pass runs synchronously in a `Scheduler::Defer` thread, or in the request when the API passes `synchronous`. A user who bypasses the client check can therefore make the server do repeated heavy conversions on large files. Consider rejecting `tempfile.size > 10.megabytes` before downsizing, so the server enforces the same limit as the client.

No tests for automatic downsizing or the new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature

`spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb` have no case where an image exceeds `max_image_size_kb` and gets downsized. They have none for the `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` signature either. A spec calling the existing `downsize(path, path, 100, 100)` form would have caught the override at `optimized_image.rb:149`.

Unsubscribe is not idempotent: a reload or second visit escalates to muted

The action computes the new level from the current one. Above regular it sets regular (lines 107-108). Otherwise it sets muted (lines 109-111). The first click from the email takes a watching or tracking user to regular. Reloading the page, pressing Back/Forward when the browser re-fetches, or opening the email link a second time then hits the `else` branch and mutes the topic. The page text is the same both times, so the user is not told. Muting is a stronger change than the email link's text promises ("stop receiving notifications"). It also hides the topic from the user's lists. The same happens if the user picks Tracking in the dropdown on this page and then reloads: they end up at regular.

A GET that changes state needs a deterministic result. For example, always set regular for levels above regular and leave regular or muted unchanged. If muting is wanted, make it an explicit second step, such as the button on the page.

`tu.save!` bypasses TopicUser.change, so reason, timestamp and MessageBus are not updated

Every other notification-level change goes through `TopicUser.change` (e.g. `set_notifications` at line 332). That method sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (default `user_changed`) and publishes `notification_level_change` on `/topic/:id` to the user (app/models/topic_user.rb:87-114). The direct `save!` does none of this.

After unsubscribing, the stored reason still describes the old state, for example auto-watch because the user posted. `notifications_changed_at` is stale. Other open tabs of the same user are not told. The route hides the reason text on the client (topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:14), which suggests the stale reason is already noticed. The same `TopicUser.change` call also creates the row when it is missing, which removes the nil case in the next finding. Consider `TopicUser.change(current_user, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`.

`tu` can be nil, giving a 500 on the unsubscribe URL

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the logged-in user has no topic_users row for the topic. Line 107 then raises NoMethodError. The notification mailer creates a row with `TopicUser.change(... last_emailed_post_number ...)` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:312), so links from emails normally have one. The route is a plain URL, though. Any logged-in user without a row (a different account than the email recipient, or a deleted row) gets a server error instead of a sensible response. Using `TopicUser.change` (see the previous finding) or handling nil would cover it.

State change on a GET with no CSRF protection `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a GET. Rails does not check the CSRF token on GET, and `check_xhr` is skipped for this action (line 32). Any page can send a logged-in user's browser to `/t/:id/unsubscribe`, by navigation or by an `` on browsers without SameSite-Lax defaults. That mutes or lowers the topic for them. The impact is low, but a confirm step on the page would avoid it. The page already renders the notifications button. The server could change state only on a PUT/POST from that page. That would also remove the repeat-visit escalation in the first finding.

Logged-out recipients are sent to the home page and nothing is unsubscribed

`unsubscribe` is behind `ensure_logged_in`. For a logged-out HTML GET, the `NotLoggedIn` handler does `redirect_to path("/")` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:97-104). It does not store `destination_url`. The `destination_url` cookie is only set in `redirect_to_login_if_required` (line 420), which applies only when login is required. People who click "click here" in an email from a mail app or a browser with no session land on the home page with no explanation. They are not unsubscribed, and after logging in they are not returned to the unsubscribe page. Consider setting `cookies[:destination_url]` for this action, or rendering the login prompt.

Client-side navigation shows "You will stop receiving notifications" without any server change

The unsubscribe only happens in the server action. The Ember route just loads the topic view and renders the text. Internal links are routed client-side by `Discourse.URL.routeTo` -> `handleURL` (lib/url.js:108-166, 313-332). A click on this URL inside the app, such as a link in a post, reaches this route without a server request for `/unsubscribe`. In that case there is no preloaded `topic_<id>` entry, so `loadTopicView` fetches `/t/:id.json`, which is `topics#show` (models/post-stream.js.es6:821-823). The user sees a page saying they will stop receiving notifications, but their level is unchanged. Consider having the route compare the notification level or call the server explicitly. Alternatively, mark the route so that links to it do a full page load.

Misspelled property name `stopNotificiationsText`

The name is spelled `Notificiations` here and in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3. It is used consistently, so nothing breaks, but it is a typo in new code. Rename it to `stopNotificationsText` in both files.

`add_unsubscribe_link: true` now requires `unsubscribe_url`, otherwise I18n raises

The English `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855). `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` at lines 67 and 90 raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when the option is absent. No tests for the new unsubscribe action, route or email content

Delete-cache action is now exposed where connection modification is disabled

Timestamp hard-codes the en-US locale

Slots on a date-override day skip the busy-time check

Working-hours check drops valid slots for split schedules and ignores the slot end

A 14:00 slot is outside the 09-12 entry, so `find` returns true and the slot is rejected. Fixed and loose hosts get their own `workingHours` through `...schedule`, so every multi-window host loses slots. The slot should be unavailable only if no entry for that day contains it. Use `some` to check containment and negate it, and only when entries exist for that day.

The check is also largely redundant: `getTimeSlots` already builds slots only inside working hours.

Override range check lets slots that straddle the override boundaries through

A slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start (line 118) or starts after the override end (line 123). A slot that starts before the override start and ends after it, or one that starts inside the override and ends after its end, is accepted. For example, an override of 09:00-12:00 accepts an 11:30 slot of 60 minutes. The conditions should be `slotStartTime.isBefore(start)` and `slotEndTime.isAfter(end)`. `getTimeSlots` mostly prevents these slots today, but this per-user check is supposed to be the guard.

The day match on lines 110-111 has two more problems. It formats `dayjs(date.start).add(...)` in the server's local timezone but formats the slot in UTC, so the two sides disagree on a non-UTC server. It also matches only the override's start date, so an override that crosses UTC midnight (an organizer in UTC+10 working 09:00-17:00) never matches the slots after midnight UTC.

Offset computation is fragile and repeated

`dayjs(override.start.toString())` round-trips a Date through its locale string, which drops milliseconds and relies on non-standard parsing. Pass `override.start` directly. Also, `override.start` is a wall-clock time stored as UTC, not the real instant. Taking the tz offset at that fake instant can be off by an hour on the day of a DST change in either zone. `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`, and `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the server's timezone. Compute `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` once per bound instead of twice.

Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but most callers expect their SDK/axios result

Also check that the decrypted `keys` is a non-null object before writing it to `credential.key`. Sync endpoint failures are not distinguished from token errors

The listener body is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1). `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever V2 is enabled (line 67). Its `clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` always throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195).

If both features are on, deleting any client fires `ClientRemovedEvent` and reaches line 91. The exception escapes the listener and client deletion fails. Both features can be on together: `TOKEN_EXCHANGE_STANDARD_V2` depends on V1 (`Profile.java:77`), and nothing makes V1 and V2 exclusive. The same combination also makes `PUT clients/{id}/management/permissions` (V1-gated, `ClientResource.java:739-742`) fail with a 500.

Before this PR, `clients()` in V2 mode was the inherited V1 class, so this combination did not throw.

Fix options: skip the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch when V2 is enabled, or make `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` a no-op. Add a test that deletes a client with the V2 feature on.

Existing V2 realms lack the Clients resource and new scopes; possible NPE/ModelException

`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226-228`). A realm that enabled V2 permissions before this PR was therefore created with only the `Users` type resource and no `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` or `map-roles-composite` scopes.

For such a realm, `getResourceTypeResource(..., "Clients")` returns null at line 217, and line 219 then calls `findByResource(server, null)`. Creating a per-client permission would hit `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:108`).

`getResourceTypeResource` also returns null when the realm's admin-permissions flag is switched off after the client exists. `UserPermissionsV2` has the same shape. Is there a migration for realms initialised before this change, or is the experimental feature allowed to break them? If not, guard the null resource at line 217 (return false).

canExchangeTo throws in V2, turning a token-exchange denial into a 500

`AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token)` whenever the audience client differs from the caller (`AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276`). With V2 enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, so this now reaches line 149 and throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. The caller gets a 500 instead of the 403 "Client not allowed to exchange" at lines 277-280.

Before this PR the inherited V1 implementation answered `false`, or evaluated V1 permissions. Is a V2 plus legacy token-exchange setup meant to be unsupported? If so, say it explicitly. Otherwise return `false` here, as the old behaviour did when no V1 permission existed.
